decision.explanation: The evidence from the phase I study of pazopanib and vorinostat in advanced solid tumors supports the claim that TP53 hotspot mutations (specifically R213*, G245S, and R273C) are associated with improved sensitivity/response in colorectal cancer. Evidence fragment f01 explicitly lists these three variants as detected in colorectal cancer cases within the study population and notes that TP53 mutation detection was associated with higher rates of stable disease (SD ≥6 months) or partial response (PR), longer median progression-free survival (PFS), and longer median overall survival (OS) compared to patients without the mutation. Evidence fragment f02 provides specific quantitative data for the subgroup of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer, showing that those with detected hotspot TP53 mutations had a significantly longer median PFS (6.5 months vs. 2.0 months) and median OS (19.8 months vs. 7.2 months) compared to TP53-undetected cases. The therapies (Pazopanib, Vorinostat), combination interaction, somatic origin (implied by 'hotspot mutation' in cancer context), and disease (Colorectal Cancer) align with the claim. The specific variants R213*, G245S, and R273C are confirmed as present in the colorectal cancer cohort of this study.

citations.quote:
In the phase I study of pazopanib and vorinostat in 36 patients with advanced solid tumors, detection of hotspot TP53 mutation was associated with a higher rate of SD ≥6 months/PR, longer median PFS (months), and longer median OS (months) compared to patients without a hotspot TP53 mutation. 
In colorectal cancer cases, detected TP53 hotspot mutations included TP53 R213*, TP53 G245S, and TP53 R273C.

In the subgroup of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer and sarcoma treated with pazopanib and vorinostat, those with detected hotspot TP53 mutations (n = 6) had a significantly longer median PFS of 6.5 months (95% CI 3.0–9.0; p = 0.023) compared to 2.0 months (95% CI 1.8–2.2; p = 0.023) in TP53-undetected cases (n = 10), and a significantly longer median OS of 19.8 months (95% CI 8.2–31.4; p = 0.021) versus 7.2 months (95% CI 0.6–13.8; p = 0.021), respectively.
